notes:
Written for batch ia-02-d. Eight pages opened (budget 5 for the Nogai row plus 9 for the Small Horde row, which this dossier absorbs; the Crimean Khanate page is shared with crimean-khanate).
DECISION ON THE SHARED WIKIDATA ID (Q631210, 'Nogai Horde' / 'Small Horde'): the two Cliopatria rows are ONE state, so this dossier lists both Names and reviews all 16 shapes (7 Nogai Horde 1450-1563, 9 Small Horde 1564-1737). Evidence: Cliopatria's Small Horde shape of 1564 (521,534 km2) contains the whole 1563 Nogai shape (0 km2 left over) plus the Kuban steppe; the later shapes shrink by the same steps the pages give (Kazakhs, Russia, Kalmyks); from 1636 only the Kuban steppe remains, the Lesser Nogai Horde of the page; the 1738 Crimean shape takes exactly that strip. The Nogai page itself says '1557 Mirza Kazy crosses the Volga and founds Small Horde along the Kuban'. Cliopatria's 'Small Horde' is NOT the Kazakh Little Juz (Kazakh page: 'the Little Horde in western Kazakhstan'), whose lands lie elsewhere. The ia-03-c brief also lists small-horde: if that agent wrote a separate small-horde dossier, the orchestrator should drop it or turn it into a stub that points here.
Settled: 1520-21 Kazakh conquest of the south-east steppe; 1557 Lesser Horde on the Kuban; 1570 Emba; 1632-34 Kalmyk conquest; capital Saray-Jük to 1577.
Unsettled: start year (Cliopatria 1450 against infobox 1480 and lead 'about 1500'; confidence 1); the capture of Saray-Juk (1520 Kazakh page, c. 1522 and 1577 Nogai page); the 1572, 1588 and 1636 steps are Cliopatria's years with the pages giving nearby but different dates (1570/1577, 1586 Samara, 1634). 'c. 1509 Nogais move into lands vacated by Great Horde' is not mapped (the page gives no outline); the Black Sea Nogais (Budjak, Yedisan, Jamboyluk, Yedickul) were 'nominally subject' to the Crimean Khanate, undated; the Nogais tribute from Kazan and Astrakhan ('Nogais lose tribute', 1552 and 1556) has no start date, so no vassal pair is written; the 1600 and 1619 civil wars are not territorial on the page. Cliopatria's Kuban strip overlaps the Crimean 1450-1571 shape by about 51,000 km2 in 1564-1571.
For other dossiers: crimean-khanate carries the matching 1572 loss and 1738 gain of the Kuban strip (counterpart nogai-horde); kazakh-khanate should carry the 1521 and 1572 gains (counterpart nogai-horde); kalmyk-khanate the 1636 gain; tsardom-of-russia the 1588 gain of the Middle Volga steppe.
Not opened (budget): Mangit, Yusuf, Ismail Bey, Siege of Astrakhan 1569, Tsaritsyn, Saratov, Ufa, Don Cossacks, Yedisan, Budjak Horde, Kuban Khanate.
Gazetteer: no place 'Saraichik'; coordinates only.

REVIEW FIXES (reviewer verdict fail; fixed 2026-10-19, pages re-opened: Nogais, Nogai Horde, Crimean Khanate, Kazakh Khanate, Kalmyk Khanate).
1. The Kuban/Azov strip in 1557-1571 now has one owner, the Crimean Khanate (option a of the review).
